pr_body:
This is another attempt to add support for vsock in grpc since previous
PRs(#24551, #21745) all closed without merging.

The VSOCK address family facilitates communication between
virtual machines and the host they are running on.
This patch will introduce new scheme: [vsock:cid:port] to
support VSOCK address family.

Fixes #32738.

<!--
PLEASE DO NOT POST A QUESTION HERE.
This form is for bug reports and feature requests ONLY!

For general questions and troubleshooting, please ask/look for answers at StackOverflow, with "grpc" tag: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/grpc

For questions that specifically need to be answered by gRPC team members, please ask/look for answers at grpc.io mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/grpc-io

Issues specific to *grpc-java*, *grpc-go*, *grpc-node*, *grpc-dart*, *grpc-web* should be created in the repository they belong to (e.g. https://github.com/grpc/grpc-LANGUAGE/issues/new)
-->

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Vsockets are not currently supported in main line grpc.

I'm aware the ChromiumOS and Android projects are using forks of GRPC to enable vsockets aka AF_VSOCK sockets, based on the patch found here:
https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/grpc-grpc/+/a0d43cf1a94bc5443ee8ee2499490f6af4da6272

It appears Android is referencing an old version of grpc:
```
version = "1.16.0-dev"
```
and I'd like to adopt a newer version. The version currently being used for my project is v1.48.1, and it's not really an option for me to go back to an earlier version.

Has there been any update since the discussion found here?
https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/25801

### Describe the solution you'd like
Either a port of the patch mentioned above for a newer version of grpc, or support for vsocks in the grpc main line.

### Describe alternatives you've considered
My other options are to use:
1. plain POSIX sockets,
2. implement a custom transport for grpc (may be out of scope for the goal),
3. or try to port the patch above to the new version of grpc.

### Additional context
I'd like to know whether the vsock support has been ported already to a newer version of grpc in any public fork, and/or whether the support for vsockets is planned. It seems multiple major projects would benefit from this, and support in the main line would reduce fragmentation in absorbing security updates.
comments: There is no vsock support in gRPC currently.  There was a previous attempt in https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/24551, but it was never finished by the contributor.  If you'd like to contribute a PR to add vsock support in a similar way, we'd be happy to review it.

> There is no vsock support in gRPC currently. There was a previous attempt in #24551, but it was never finished by the contributor. If you'd like to contribute a PR to add vsock support in a similar way, we'd be happy to review it.

review_comments: I believe this is missing some includes since they are all inside the `GRPC_HAVE_VSOCK` guard. You could manually compile with the flag disabled to check for these things.
I have tried remove `GRPC_HAVE_VSOCK` from `src/core/lib/iomgr/port.h`, the build still passed.  I think required includes already in `src/core/lib/iomgr/vsock.h`

That's interesting. IWYU would normally complain that this file does not have all the required includes directly, but maybe the tool can't see that because of the ifdef guards. In that case, if the CI is happy, this can be left as is.

@veblush Please provide guidance on whether new code return absl::Status or `grpc_error_handle`. It seems `GRPC_ERROR_CREATE` will still be helpful in the future since it captures file & line automatically, but it's unclear if `grpc_error_to_absl_status` should be used with the resulting Status.

My hunch is that this should return absl::Status, and that grpc_error_to_absl_status is unnecessary.

Although `UnixAbstractSockaddrPopulate` appears to use `grpc_error_handle`, we can use `absl::Status` instead here as we're recommended to use it if possible. `absl::Status` is still having debug-location for debug build so simply using `absl::Status` would be recommended. If capturing file & line number is a must, we can do it manually by adding `GRPC_DEFAULT_FILE` and `GRPC_DEFAULT_LINE` to the message but I guess it isn't.
Correction on the error information; You need to use `grpc_core::StatusCreate` or `GRPC_ERROR_CREATE` macro variants to get debug information. `absl::Status` alone doesn't do it.

I thought about this, but since the other code in this file still uses the old status APIs, it seems fine for this code to do the same thing.  At some point we'll want to modernize all of the code in this file, but until then we might as well be consistent.

I would love it if someone wants to dive in and modernize this code, including moving all of it to idiomatic C++ APIs instead of old style C APIs.  But I didn't want to hold up this feature on that work.
I have no strong opinion here, fine to leave as is. Thank you for the guidance regardless, Esun, that will be helpful going forward.
You need to include `src/core/lib/iomgr/port.h` before this line for `GRPC_HAVE_VSOCK` to be defined.
yes, I will move the `#include "src/core/lib/iomgr/port.h"` to `parse_address.h`
uhmm, the auto-fix(https://github.com/YadongQi/grpc/pull/18/files) suggest to move it back... how to handle this?

Given that the methods in this header are only defined if `#ifdef GRPC_HAVE_VSOCK` in the `cc` file, I'd suggest adding the same check here under the port_platform include.

I mean to say that this header should also have those guards. If any code is attempting to use these functions when `GRPC_HAVE_VSOCK` is not defined, then it will be a compile time error instead of a linker error.

```
#ifndef GRPC_SRC_CORE_LIB_IOMGR_VSOCK_H
#define GRPC_SRC_CORE_LIB_IOMGR_VSOCK_H

#include <grpc/support/port_platform.h>

#include "src/core/lib/iomgr/port.h"

#ifdef GRPC_HAVE_VSOCK

// code goes here

#endif
#endif  /* GRPC_SRC_CORE_LIB_IOMGR_VSOCK_H */
```
That will work fine, thanks.

Sorry I didn't notice this on the last review pass. AF_VSOCK may not be defined, right? I believe the rest are guaranteed to exist on all the posix platforms we support. I think the relevant #include should be added to this file, and that this should be guarded by `#ifdef GRPC_HAVE_VSOCK`.

do you mean to add below code in sockaddr_posix.h also? if so, I can remove all include from all other cc files like vsock.cc/sock_addr_utils.cc.... 
```
#ifdef GRPC_HAVE_VSOCK
#include <linux/vm_sockets.h>
#endif
```
But it seems not aligned with AF_UNIX, for all other cc files reference AF_UNIX, it needs to include "sys/un.h" before include sockaddr.h. I am not sure whether need to broke this rule? could you confirm this?

Good question, it looks inconsistent already. Most of the types used in this file are from either `sys/socket.h` or `arpa/inet.h`, which are included in this file. I _think_ the best thing to do is to conditionally include the vsock headers here, define `GRPC_AF_VSOCK` unconditionally, and wrap all uses of `GRPC_AF_VSOCK` in `#ifdef GRPC_HAVE_VSOCK`. Then all files that need to use AF_VSOCK will only have to wrap the usage in guards, not the includes.
